goal: VC-201-100 (P1) claims mastery of: On isolated local and explicitly configured cloud environments, configure the ecosystem, run and recover a swarm mission, evaluate a self-patch, and promote only through the tagged release path; publish reproducible scorecard deltas and remaining limitations, including a 2x improvement claim only if its predeclared metric and evidence support it.. Its own narrative does not claim delivery: PARTIAL: qualification covers the tagged release path and gates a 2x improvement claim on its evidence. Verified by `crates/susi-gawd/src/tests/vc_201_100.rs`: qualifies_tagged_path_and_gates_2x_claim. Residual: the full multi-stage qualification - configuring the ecosystem, running and recovering a swarm mission, evaluating a self-patch on isolated local and explicitly configured cloud environmen. Prove or refute it: add a nonzero test named vc_201_100_mastery_* that exercises the capability on its production path, and record exactly which part is missing when it cannot be proven. Coverage is not mastery: this closes only when the capability is verified, and a linked closed task is not evidence. Closing this task records the outcome, not a passing test: write .agents/roadmap-verdicts/<the vector>.json with verdict 'delivered' (and the test or record that proves it) or 'not-delivered' (with what is missing and the task ids that track the follow-up work), then run scripts/check-roadmap-verdict.py <the vector> — which is this task's acceptance. A refutation therefore closes the task and files the work, instead of stalling on a test that cannot pass; the roadmap and the queue both understand the record. Do not reserve .agents/roadmap-verdicts in your claim: the directory is exempt from the scope check precisely so a verdict commits under your source claim, and reserving it would overlap every other verification task and serialize them all. Reserve the source paths you will touch, and add a scope if the verdict needs to change the vector's narrative in .agents/roadmap.json. Evidence must name something real: a path that exists in the checkout, or an identifier (a test name) that appears in it. The checker verifies this, so a verdict cannot be closed by typing a claim.
